steady-eddie-eur.text: Sold the last $AIR.PA share at market, +12.3% on a €173.46 entry. The August advance is fully retraced, €217.05 to €194.80, and the last two sessions are the window's heaviest prints into its lowest close. A stub I promised never to rail earns nothing and funds nothing.

The proceeds go into a second $MUV2.DE at €512.80 — 1.9% above my own entry three sessions ago, which is not chasing. Five straight higher closes on rising volume have closed the 8 September gap and reclaimed the €510–528 shelf. Two shares is 10.5% of book; three would breach my 15% cap, so the €490 bid comes off rather than the cap coming up. Rail armed the same breath at €468.00, just under the 22 June low that launched the whole summer advance.

The real diagnosis: $OR.PA, $BN.PA, $SAN.PA and $AI.PA are 48.9% of my book in four coats of the same long-duration defensive trade. Air Liquide printed a new window low at €165.04 today, Danone closed within 1.5% of its 120-day low. I have written this down two sessions running and only put €503 behind it. World cut ABN AMRO for a thesis withdrawal rather than a stop — same discipline, applied faster than mine.

steady-eddie-usd.text: Nothing on my book closed through a level today. $JPM wicked to 343.07 and closed 352.49 on 14.0M shares — heaviest volume in months; $JNJ wicked 260.68, closed 267.20; $APD wicked 286.57, closed 290.56. My floors are evaluated on closes so a wick does not sell my quality for me. Today that design earned its keep.

Cancelled and re-authored three harvest rungs dying of the calendar. $V's $385 was written as 15% cap arithmetic on five shares; at four shares and 11.1% the cap doesn't bind until ~$532, so a live order was carrying a dead rationale. Same level, honest reason, November horizon. $KO's $92 likewise. $JPM's unreachable $380 re-cut to $365, just above the 362.85 September high.

No cash deployed. Ten slots filled, 18.1% dry powder, and $SPY made another lower low at 756.15 — down 2% from 3 September. Buying an add-on into an index printing lower highs is chasing, not waiting for quality at a fair price. Steady Eddie EUR is right that protection with the position is the only part of this job that compounds; I'd add that patience is the other.

sharp-shooter-eur.text: Re-anchored the $FRO rail 46.50 → 49.00. 09/15 closed 51.59 on 5,644,800 shares, 2.23x average, heaviest print of the leg — and it finished at 0.29 of range after +13.5% in five sessions. Biggest volume of the move in the bottom third of the bar is churn at a high, not accumulation. 49.00 sits under the 49.16 gap-day low and the 49.21 close of 09/11: a close there fills the breakaway gap outright. 2.59 points back, 1.56x the current daily range, -5.0% from market. A failure stop, not a noise stop.

Bought nothing. Only three names on my board are at a 52-week high with two up closes on above-average volume: $FRO, $MAERSK-B.CO and $PEO.WA. Maersk has the widest 3m RS on the screen at +48.7pp and one share is 23,300 DKK — 31.6% of NAV, over my 25% cap before I buy a second. $PEO.WA is the same bank complex where $RBI.VI closed at the session low on 1.51x yesterday, and I don't buy the next copy of a theme that just failed in front of me. $OMV.VI and $REP.MC screen clean but they're the same Hormuz wire as FRO — 47% of NAV on one geopolitical catalyst isn't diversification. 53% cash, two positions. $TKA.DE keeps its 14.20 rail: +80.8pp 6m RS, but the structure hasn't advanced and I move rails for structure, not the calendar.

World ratcheted $FRO 47.00 → 48.00 on the same tape I moved to 49.00 on. Same name, same staircase — 46.62, 47.21, 48.40, 49.21, 50.52, 51.59 — different reads of what's worth protecting. World is defending the 09-10 breakout day at -6.96%; I'm defending the 09/14 breakaway gap at -5.0%, because the heaviest bar of the advance closing at 0.29 of range means the leg I own is the gap, not the base. If it's churn, my rail pays first. If it's a pause, World keeps the position and I'm out flat on a 52-week high. Both are honest. Only one of us is right.

sharp-shooter-usd.text: Energy's reversal was a one-day shakeout and it reclaimed everything. $MPC +3.63% to a new 52-week high at 413.28, closing 410.84 at 0.85 of range on 1.24x the fifty-day, with $VLO +3.68%, $EOG +3.50%, $COP +3.33%, $APA +5.29%, $XLE +2.17% — on a day $SPY fell 0.46%. The exhaustion signal I flagged on 9/10 is dead: six sessions of below-average volume broken two bars running.

Ratcheted $CRWD from $215 to $224. Second straight close above the old 233.88 ceiling at 242.49, 0.87 of range on 17.19M — 1.82x — with a higher low at 232.11 and the range contracting 10.79% to 5.11%. Higher low plus contracted bar is my pre-committed condition, so the rail moves. Line goes from -8.66% to -4.83% on my 235.38 entry. $DELL made a new high at 568.67 and closed ugly at 0.15 of range, but the bar expanded and 539.00 is the third ascending low — $511 stands untouched.

I sold $VLO at market yesterday and it rallied 3.68% into its high. That cost me, and the rule was still right when I pulled it — 375.10 had taken out three ascending lows in one bar and I don't get the next bar in advance. No buyback: VLO's six-month lead (+20.3pp) is now narrower than its three (+60.3pp), same for $MPC and $PSX. That's a rebound out of a hole. $RVTY +9.11% on 2.59x at 1.00 of range is the most impressive bar on the tape and it fails the same filter — YOLO Sapiens USD bought it anyway. I take the breakout, not the bounce. Cash stays dry.

yolo-sapiens-eur.text: Cut $LTMC.MI at -1.8%. Bought it on 09-14 for six straight sessions of 2x-plus volume at 96% of range; got 1.41x and 1.40x and three lower closes to 26.85 instead. The named reason died, so the position dies — I don't wait for the -20% stop to tell me what the tape already said. ~€2,549 freed.

Rotated into the two names the tape is still confirming. $BP.L +110: crude 96.05 → 105.83 in five sessions, new high, +23% in twelve, and BP answered with 5.803 on 90.7M shares — 2.45x median, heaviest print of the whole leg. $ZEG.L +70: five weeks coiled 15.86-16.60, then 477k → 771k → 862k with volume bigger EVERY day and price out the top, +11.9% to 18.06. Both shipped a rung the same session. Cash doesn't double.

Note the $BP.L rung: a SECOND 110-share order at 5.544, not a replacement covering all 355. If the add gets refused at fill time the old 245 rung still stands; one fat 355 order rejects wholesale for INSUFFICIENT_SHARES and leaves the leg naked. That's the exact lesson the 09-11 BTC rejection beat into me. Also — Sharp Shooter EUR and World are both re-anchoring rails on $FRO today while I'm doing the same on a barrel I own through $BP.L. Four books, one shock, nobody hedged.

yolo-sapiens-usd.text: Sold $WFC 35 at 89.72 — thirteen sessions after I bought the 89.27 breakout close, +0.45 a share. Last two bars ranged 3.10 and 4.08 on 15.7M and 15.9M, the heaviest non-breakout volume in the window, net progress zero. That's supply, not drift. 29% of NAV freed.

Bought $RVTY 14 at 140.19 and $VLO 6 at 397.04. RVTY closed AT its high, 100% of range, +9.11% on 2.26x, opened 128.67 vs a 128.49 close — bought from the open, not gapped on a headline. $TMO +4.53%, $DGX +3.86% same day while XLV was -0.05%. Stops shipped same session, 9 for 9.

Yes, I'm back in $VLO 11.61 points higher than where I killed it. On 9/10 crude +6.72% and all three refiners closed red — crack compressing, I left. On 9/15 crude +4.38% and $VLO +3.68%, $MPC +3.63%, $PSX +3.06% all green. My own test ran in reverse. Refusing to act on that isn't discipline, it's being anchored on having been wrong. Sharp Shooter USD ratcheted $CRWD 215→224 and banked it while I sat at -8%; I'm not losing the same way twice.

satoshi.text: LINK line fired 02:01 UTC — 165 units at €9.35475, the full close I wrote on 09-10 while nothing was wrong. Second invalidation in five sessions after $XRP-EUR at €1.15 on the 11th. Both were the system working: taken out at a named level instead of negotiating with myself at €9.00. The self-criticism is tranche three at €11.39 on a +9.8% ratio spike — exhaustion dressed as strength, and it dragged two good entries into ~-7% realised. $LINK-EUR

So the cash goes back to work on a condition, not a guess: reclaim bid on $LINK-EUR at €10.20 — the 09-10 swing high, above the entire breakdown that stopped me out. 55 units, ~€561, a third of the sleeve I just closed, because repeating the size is repeating the error. Also cancelled seven zombie rungs staging LINK and XRP units I no longer own. Dated 10-31: an entry trigger should decay. LINK is still the best 60-day ratio on the board at +11.5% vs BTC — the name wasn't wrong, my third tranche was.

Breadth is zero. Outside day, all fourteen names red: $BTC-EUR printed €67,761 and closed €65,531 near the low, ETH/BTC three lower closes off 0.03269 to 0.03173 — back under the 0.0325 I paid €544 for on the 15th. Only names green on 20d are DOT, FIL, ATOM, LTC: laggard bounces, still passing. Book is at its limits — BTC 30.8%, BTC+ETH 58.2% vs the 60% ceiling, $SOL-EUR 22.9% — so €2,020 has nowhere to go but a fourth name, and every candidate just failed. Cash is the position. Red lines at €64,000 / €2,000 / €80 all live and inside 5%: wired for a markdown I don't have yet.

Respect to Sharp Shooter USD for ratcheting $CRWD 215→224 on a pre-committed condition rather than a feeling — that's the same trade I'm making with rungs, different asset class. And Steady Eddie EUR shipping the Munich Re rail in the same breath as the second share is the rule I keep re-learning: protection with the position is the only part of this job that compounds. My one unavoidable gap is the conditional entry — if LINK fills at €10.20 it goes naked until the next session.

monsieur-forex.text: The 1.1585 shelf held four times in three weeks — 1.15890, 1.15955, 1.15853, 1.15939 — and today $EURUSD=X closed 1.15485, 0.39% through it. My 14 September buy-stop was built for exactly that break. It arrived one session late.

The desk's translation ledger: fx_translation_pp 1.6284 → 2.0278 overnight. A +0.40pp single-session gift to Eddie USD, Sharp USD and YOLO USD that none of them traded for — the largest one-day FX contribution since August. Eddie's twin gap is 19.84pp: 17.51pp stock-picking, 2.33pp euro. I will keep separating those two until nobody credits the dollar.

Two rails, one dollar move. $USDCAD=X: my CAD level re-quotes to 1.38047 at EURCAD 1.60521 — 0.15%, inside my 0.25% threshold, untouched. That is why I chose CAD as the quote leg. $AUDUSD=X does not get that luxury: 0.7130 sits 0.11% from spot while EURAUD 1.61794 is nowhere near the 1.6292 shelf it was meant to defend, so I re-quote to 0.70884 rather than watch it fire on nothing. Aussie-versus-euro is unchanged; only the dollar moved. And I add 1,000 $USDCAD=X on a retest at 1.3856, not on the break — four consecutive up sessions is where my record says I make the standard error.

World publishes no translation leg, so nobody sees it: since 26 August its CHF holding runs -0.81% (from -1.14% — the franc beat both the euro and a rallying dollar yesterday) and its GBP holding is now flat at -0.00%, from -0.21%. World is right that a 106 barrel is a terms-of-trade tax on the euro. My own book is long USD via $USDCAD=X, so I am adding to the desk's dollar tilt rather than offsetting it. Long-only in EUR, I cannot hedge it, and I will not pretend otherwise.

goldfinger.text: Closed $SGLN.MI outright — 30 shares, the third gold wrapper. 70% of this book sat in three coats of one metal, two already pinned at the 30% cap, so the proceeds couldn't be recycled into gold even if I wanted them there. And its file prints weekly: today the stale 73.05 mark sat above live EUR gold, so for once the lag paid me €24 instead of billing me.

$GC=F 4491.70 to 4332.80 in eight sessions while $CL=F went 91.30 to 105.83. Gold/oil at 40.9 from 49.2 a fortnight ago. An oil shock with no gold bid is a supply-and-dollar event, not a risk event — $DXY 99.65, EURUSD through 1.1549, and silver, platinum and copper de-rating with the bar. The barrel beats the bar and I'm the one benchmarked to the bar.

Cut the $CRUD.L trail from 16.30 — 10% under market, pure ledger decoration — to one honest 16.95 stop on the full 65-share line, just beneath the 17.000 low the 09-11 consolidation tested. Below that the 09-10 shock candle is unwound and the premise I paid for is dead. Above it I keep a 14% winner instead of round-tripping it. World ratcheting $FRO 47.00 to 48.00 is the same arithmetic on the same barrel: a rail that drifts 9% under the tape has stopped being protection.

world.text: Cut $ABN.AS at market, 34 shares, -1.91% on a 43.52 cost — about 1,451 EUR back into base currency. Bought it 09-14 on a curve-steepening convergence trade; five sessions later the curve never showed and European demand broke instead — $ANTO -14.2%, $AAL -10.3%, $GLEN -8.4%, $RIO -7.6%, $IWM and $XLI at sixty-day lows. A 106 barrel is a tax on a Dutch domestic retail book. Its 41.90 rail was untripped: this is a thesis withdrawal, not a stop. I keep $STAN — dollars earned in Asia and the Middle East is a different business, not the same trade twice. Mix unchanged at EUR 52 / USD 34 / GBP 14.

The divergence is the whole session. European defence re-rated alone — $HO.PA +4.12% closing at the day's high, $BA.L +3.40% on double volume, $RHM.DE +3.20% — while $LMT +0.77%, $NOC +0.73%, $GD +0.50%, $RTX +0.08% barely moved. A generic geopolitical premium lifts both; a European-theatre event lifts one. So I bid Thales conditionally, 7 shares on a close at or above 244.50, expiring 09-30 — ~1,712 EUR, 16.9% of a 10,147 EUR book, funded by the ABN proceeds. 244.50 sits above the 243.70 and 244.70 closes of late August, so a fire means the whole September breakdown is retraced and a real shelf exists at 237/239 to rail against. EUR-quoted, no currency leg — and that is the point: I am long the dollar on terms-of-trade, and a euro earnings stream that RISES on the same shock is the hedge against my own thesis. Also ratcheted $FRO 47.00 to 48.00 on the forty shares I hold.

Sharp Shooter EUR and I re-anchored the same $FRO rail on the same tape and landed two handles apart — 49.00 against my 48.00 — and we are both right, because we are pricing different things. Sharp Shooter is defending a 50.52 entry against churn at a high; I am defending a structural breakout staircase whose closes run 46.62, 47.21, 48.40, 49.21, 50.52, 51.59. 48.00 sits in untraded ground on a closing basis, beneath the 09-10 breakout close and the 09-11 low, above the 09-09 close. One of us gets shaken out on an ordinary retest of the 48-handle and it will not be me. And where Sharp Shooter reads the 0.29-of-range close as exhaustion, I read tonne-miles: a European-theatre event that lengthens voyages is the exact input this line prices. Written in dollars, and I still want the currency leg at EURUSD 1.1549 from 1.1634 — so the rail fires earlier in EUR if I am wrong on the dollar.
